_comment: Tier-2 for sparta hypersonic_flow and adaptive_grid: a uniform grid sized on freestream conditions is far too coarse at the shock, and refining on particle count does not fix it. Three decks were run on the installed binary (SPARTA 24 Sep 2025, spa_serial), identical but for the 'fix adapt' line: a physically scaled Mach-5 argon flow past a cylinder. The scaling is deliberate — upstream examples/circle uses nrho 1.0, which makes the flow free molecular with cell Knudsen numbers around 1e18 and leaves nothing to resolve; here the freestream mean free path is a fraction of a cell. hypersonic_flow:3 — the cell Knudsen minimum from 'compute lambda/grid ... knall' with 'compute reduce min' is 0.0163, far below 1, and the run exits 0 with no error and no warning. adaptive_grid:4 — refining on particle count leaves the Knudsen minimum at 0.947 of its pre-adaptation value (i.e. no improvement) while refining on the Knudsen column raises it 3.19x. THRESHOLD BUNDLING CORRECTED: the entry's Signal read 'the cell Knudsen minimum has not improved EVEN THOUGH Ngrid has grown several-fold'. The first half holds and the second does not. Refining on particle count splits a cell's particles among its children, dropping them below the threshold at once, so the criterion is self-limiting: the cell count grows 1.25x, not several-fold, while the Knudsen-driven run on the same deck grows 5.6x. An agent looking for several-fold growth AND no improvement would not find the first half and could wrongly conclude the entry did not apply. The entry was corrected in the same commit. Both ratios were measured on two seeds before any gate here was chosen — particle-driven 0.947 and 0.928, Knudsen-driven 3.19 and 3.08 — and the gates (1.1 and 2.0) sit far from both clusters, which is how a Monte-Carlo quantity has to be bounded. No measured value is pinned. COVERS: hypersonic_flow:3, adaptive_grid:4. MUTATION CONTROL (added 2026-08-06, re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 gives the 'particle count' deck the SAME Knudsen refinement criterion the control deck uses and changes nothing else — same seed, same 200-step adapt interval, same maxlevel 3. Because the wrong-criterion deck then IS the right-criterion deck, the comparison is not merely perturbed, it is collapsed exactly: measured, the particle-driven Knudsen gain moves from 0.9469 to 3.189 and the cell growth from 1.248 to 5.62, both identical to the Knudsen-driven deck's 3.189 and 5.62 to the last digit, so the stochastic noise floor is removed from the comparison by construction rather than argued about. The common pre-adaptation reference, 0.0162661, is unchanged. Verified: unmutated the fixture PASSES (rc=0); with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS (rc=1) and these expect_in_output strings go False and disappear: refining_on_particle_count_does_NOT_improve_the_knudsen_minimum=True, the_particle_count_criterion_is_self_limiting_not_several_fold=True. The hypersonic_flow:3 assertions (under-resolved and silent) are properties of the unadapted baseline deck, are deliberately outside the hook, and stay True. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/sparta/adapting_on_particle_count_targets_the_wrong_cells && python source.py (passes, rc=0), then T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py (fails, rc=1). Needs a SPARTA binary: the fixtures find spa_serial/spa_mpi on PATH or at ~/Schreibtisch/sparta/src/spa_serial, else set SPARTA_BINARY; with none present they exit 0 on a SKIP: line.
_vacuity_fix: The no-binary path prints 'SKIP: no SPARTA binary found' and exits 0, and SKIP: was not forbidden — so on a machine without SPARTA this fixture PASSED having verified nothing. 'SKIP:' added to forbid_in_output so an absent binary records a failure instead of a false pass. Same defect knowledge/kratos-sparta fixed in generators_execute_on_installed_build; the gate found eight more.
